newsitem.title: USA: Furniture Brands sees higher Q3 results.
newsitem.headline: Furniture Brands sees higher Q3 results.

text.p: Furniture Brands Inc said Friday it expects to report 1996 third quarter earnings, before an extraordinary charge related to the refinancing of a secured credit agreement, of $0.21 a share, up from $0.12 earned in the same period a year ago.

Furniture Brands also said it estimates its 1996 third quarter sales will increase about six percent from last year's third qurter on a proforma basis, assuming the company's December 29, 1995 acquisition of Thomasville Furniture Industries had occurred on January 1, 1995.
The company estimates sales for the nine months will increase between four and five percent from last year assuming Thomasville had been acquired at the begining of 1995.
Net earnings before the extraordinary charge will be $0.58 compared with $0.42 in the nine months of 1995, a 38 percent increase, the company said in a statement.
Furniture Brands said its order backlog at September 30, 1996 stood at $213.5 million, a 9.4 percent increase over the previous year, pro forma for the acquisition of Thomasville.

Results for the three and nine months ended September 30, 1996 will include an extraordinary charge of $7.4 million related to a previously announced September 1996 refinancing of the company's secured credit agreement. The refinancing will result in a substantial reduction in interest expense.
At current debt levels, Furniture Brands said the lower interest costs will favorably affect annual results by about $3.7 million or $0.05 to $0.06 a share.

Furniture Brands, which makes and markets residential furniture under the Broyhill, Lane and Thomasville brand names, reported 1995 third quarter sales of $258.6 million and nine months sales of $794.8 million. These results exclude Thomasville.
Shares of Furniture Brands were trading off 3/4 to 13-7/8.
